body: Braemar Hotels & Resorts Inc. (NYSE: BHR), a Dallas-based REIT focused on luxury hotels and resorts, settled a dispute with its largest stockholder, Al Shams Investments Limited, a Bermuda company. The Cooperation and Settlement Agreement is dated October 6, 2026; Ashford Hospitality Trust, Inc. and Ashford Inc. also signed, and Al Shams's beneficial owner signed for limited purposes. Braemar filed the agreement with a Form 8-K on October 8, 2026, and a company press release that day announced it alongside a portfolio update that included the previously announced $372 million sale of the Four Seasons Resort Scottsdale.

The agreement's recitals describe what was resolved. Al Shams had nominated a slate of directors for the 2026 annual meeting. It had asserted or threatened direct claims against the company group, including defamation and libel claims, claims under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and claims similar to those brought by another investor and Morning View Hotels BH1, LLC. It had also asserted or threatened derivative claims alleging fiduciary breaches by the board and management, and was pursuing a verified petition under Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 202 to depose two former Braemar directors before filing suit. The company group denies wrongdoing, and no party admits liability.

Braemar agreed to pay $25 million for the settlement and releases plus $15 million to reimburse Al Shams's expenses, $40 million in all, payable as $20 million on signing and $10 million each four and eight months later. Each installment is conditioned on Al Shams's continued compliance. Disputes over a claimed breach go to expedited JAMS arbitration in Dallas, and a final finding of material breach requires Al Shams to return everything paid. If cash is short, Braemar may pay up to $4 million of the later installments in common stock, and the board must grant an exception to the 9.8 percent ownership limit if needed.

Al Shams withdrew its nominations, agreed to dismiss the Rule 202 petition with prejudice, and accepted a 10-year standstill barring proxy contests, share purchases and litigation or pre-suit discovery against the companies and their current and former directors and officers, except to enforce the agreement. It must vote with the board's recommendations and may consult with Braemar's search firm on candidates for one board seat, with the board retaining sole discretion. Both sides exchanged releases and agreed not to disparage each other.

In the 8-K, Braemar said it expects its own contribution to be $4 million to $6 million after insurance proceeds and Ashford's share; under a separate Allocation Agreement, Braemar and Ashford each bear 50 percent of the payments net of insurance. Braemar cautioned that it may not recover the insurance proceeds and said its contribution would likely be less than the cost of the litigation it avoided. The press release said the 2026 annual meeting will be held December 21, 2026. In a later 8-K filed November 10, 2026, Braemar reported that its advisory agreement with Ashford terminated that day as part of its move to self-management.
